articles.title: Safeguarding global terrestrial vertebrate species from future sea level rise
articles.desc: Sea-level rise (SLR) threatens terrestrial biodiversity, yet its spatiotemporal and species-specific impacts remain unclear. Integrating relative SLR projections across five Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) with Area of Habitat (AOH) maps for 34,120 terrestrial vertebrate species, we project species exposed to SLR will increase from up to 13,680 in 2050 to 15,324 by 2100, including 57-63% of birds, 47-52% of mammals, 28-36% of reptiles, and 20-24% of amphibians. In Southeast Asia, inland inundation areas support high richness. Under SSP5-8.5, species facing >10% habitat inundation surges from 18 in 2050 to 109 by 2100, with reptiles and already threatened species overrepresented. Safeguarding SLR refugia, the non-inundated habitats for exposed species, is critical, yet over 96% lie outside protected areas, demanding early international action.

articles.title: Prioritizing reducing impacts on species to minimize residual reserves
articles.desc: International conservation goals have driven rapid expansion of protected areas. This growth has favored quantity over quality, and often results in residual reserves (i.e., areas where species already experience minimal anthropogenic impact). Spatial prioritization is commonly used to help design protected area networks that represent species while minimizing costs to stakeholders. This approach can result in the siting of protected areas that do not decrease impacts on species of conservation concern. Here, we show how measures of cumulative impacts on species can be used in a spatial prioritization to site protected areas to reduce impacts on species of conservation concern. We use a trait-based vulnerability framework and anthropogenic stressor maps to quantify cumulative impacts from four human activities, and incorporate those impacts into spatial prioritizations. We demonstrate that the inclusion of cumulative impacts on species in spatial prioritization can more efficiently protect biodiversity, balance socioeconomic objectives, and avoid residual reserve outcomes.

articles.title: Unwilling to leave, unable to stay: mechanism of plasticity in site fidelity as a rewarding tactic in changing environments
articles.desc: Context Home-ranging is common among animal species, as site fidelity facilitates cognitive map development and promotes efficient habitat use. The adaptive value of site fidelity, however, should decline as habitat conditions change, yet empirical evidence remains limited, especially for wide-ranging species. Objectives We investigated how fire and forest harvesting affect home-range stability in boreal caribou, a species typically exhibiting strong site fidelity. We then identified conditions where fidelity increases mortality and when shifting home ranges becomes advantageous. Methods We monitored 331 GPS-collared caribou across 667,000 km 2 of boreal forest.

articles.title: Community-led design of nature-based solutions for mangroves in Placencia, Belize
articles.desc: Context Although mangrove nature-based solutions are important for climate mitigation, coastal resilience, and livelihood support, implementation remains constrained by the lack of relevant evidence linking ecosystem conditions to benefits for people. Objectives We developed a collaborative framework to co-design mangrove nature-based solutions in Placencia, Belize, to identify community-prioritized areas for mangrove restoration and protection and quantify the ecosystem service benefits associated with these priorities. Methods We combined participatory mapping with high-resolution habitat mapping to define priority restoration and protection areas.

articles.title: Integrating land-use and climate connectivity to link protected areas at the country level
articles.desc: Context Ecological corridors that are high in biodiversity potential and stable under climate change are central to long-term conservation planning. Yet spatial prioritization frameworks rarely integrate land-use resistance and climate stability into a unified approach, limiting their operational value for landscape management and policy. Objectives We aimed to develop an ecological connectivity framework that jointly incorporates land-use resistance and climate stability to map linkages among protected areas, and to quantify and communicate methodological uncertainty arising from key parameterization choices. Methods We applied the framework to Portugal's terrestrial protected-area network. Using a full factorial design, we varied land-use resistance, climate resistance, and dispersal capacity across multiple weightings to generate optimized linkage solutions. Selection-frequency maps derived from these solutions fed a second optimization round, producing an ensemble connectivity solution and buffered corridors. Results Individual solutions covered 0.74% of Portugal's unprotected land; the ensemble covered 0.07%, rising to 2.3% after a 1 km buffer. articles.title: Newly planted woodlands improve connectivity for woodland fauna, flora and fungi
articles.desc: Context Young planted woodlands may only support a small proportion of the biodiversity found in mature woodlands but may play an important role in promoting species movements and enhancing biodiversity due to their emerging structural similarities. Objectives We assessed whether recently planted woodlands increase connectivity between mature woodland patches relative to agricultural fields, and whether responses vary across active (small mammals, ground invertebrates) and passive (plants, fungi) dispersers. Methods We used a multi-taxa natural experiment across paired sites where mature woodlands were either connected by planted woodland or separated by farmland. Movement was quantified using PIT-tagging of small mammals and beetles, pitfall trapping, vegetation surveys, airborne spore traps and soil eDNA metabarcoding. A Bayesian beta-binomial model estimated taxon-specific habitat preferences for dispersal. Results Although we did not detect inter-patch movements, we detected higher movement of wood mice, ground active invertebrates, plants, and fungi into new woodlands relative to agricultural fields, whereas, field voles exhibited minimal movement, and some airborne fungal groups showed reduced movement within planted woodlands. articles.title: Riparian vegetation connectivity and composition jointly shape larval aquatic insect diversity across local and regional scales
articles.desc: Context Riparian vegetation is a major driver of freshwater biodiversity; however, the structural degradation of riparian vegetation due to anthropogenic pressures poses a major threat to riverine ecosystems worldwide. Objectives This study examined how riparian vegetation connectivity and composition jointly shape aquatic insect communities. We specifically asked whether connectivity and forest type have distinct effects on local and regional diversity. Methods We conducted field surveys of Ephemeroptera, Plecoptera, and Trichoptera (EPT) at 198 sites across the Yangtze River Basin. Sites were classified by riparian connectivity degree, and deciduous and natural forest cover were quantified using high-resolution remote sensing data. Results Our results revealed that increased vegetation connectivity enhanced α-diversity by promoting adult dispersal and the stability of larval habitats. articles.title: Optimizing ecological security patterns in western Jilin, China: comparative ecological source identification and explainable machine-learning resistance modeling
articles.desc: Agricultural expansion and landscape fragmentation are altering ecological connectivity in agro-pastoral transition zones. Ecological security patterns can support landscape conservation and restoration, but their reliability is constrained by uncertainty in ecological source identification and resistance surface construction. This study identified suitable methods for constructing ecological security patterns in ecologically fragile agricultural landscapes. We compared three ecological source identification approaches and five machine learning models for resistance surface construction, and assessed their implications for ecological network optimization in western Jilin, China. We assessed five ecosystem services and compared ordered weighted averaging, morphological spatial pattern analysis, and ecosystem service significance assessment for ecological source identification. We compared five machine learning models to construct the ecological resistance surface. Based on the selected sources and resistance surface, we used minimum cumulative resistance and circuit theory to identify corridors, pinch points, and barriers. Ecosystem services showed spatial heterogeneity, with most services decreasing from east to west. articles.title: Regional tree migration outpaces local migration due to fragmentation and life history traits
articles.desc: Predictions of tree species range shifts have emphasized regional migration rates, while how local migration drives regional migration remains poorly understood. Landscape fragmentation is a major source of migration lag, but its interactions with species life history traits remain understudied. We aimed to clarify mechanisms underlying differences between local and regional migration rates, quantify how fragmentation and life history traits jointly shape migration, and assess temporal variation in these effects. We quantified local and regional migration rates of temperate tree species with contrasting life history traits across fragmented landscapes. LANDIS PRO incorporated key demographic processes, including seed dispersal, colonization, establishment, growth, and mortality. We assessed direct and interactive effects of fragmentation over short (0–30 years), medium (30–65 years), and long (65–100 years) timescales. Regional migration was nearly five times faster than local migration, and increasing fragmentation reduced regional migration and increased migration lags. Fragmentation more strongly constrained regional migration, whereas, among the six focal species, life history traits such as maturity age and seed production showed stronger associations with local migration. articles.desc: Climate change and anthropogenic stressors are degrading coastal biogenic habitats, disrupting the vital pathways fish use to shift from nearshore nurseries to offshore reef environments. Although fishes are critical for ecosystem health, spatial management rarely accounts for the interconnectedness of fish habitat needs across their life cycle. To examine and compare drivers of habitat use for subadult size classes of five habitat-shifting fishes from two feeding guilds: mesopredators and herbivores. To assess the multi-species suitability of existing management zones. We used MaxEnt to model habitat suitability for our focal fishes across the Florida Keys, USA, and performed permutation analyses to compare habitat use patterns and drivers among species. We used predicted suitability maps to quantify suitability for 58 management zones. Benthic habitat type was the strongest driver, with patch- and aggregate-reefs emerging as the most suitable across species. Habitats were more moderately suitable for mesopredators across the nearshore-offshore gradient, while S. guacamaia stood out among the herbivores as preferring nearshore and mid-channel habitats over offshore habitats. articles.title: Legacy effects of land use land cover change on species distribution dynamics: evidence from a landscape of diverse biogeographic crossroads
articles.desc: Context Land use and land cover (LULC) change is a key driver of biodiversity distribution, yet species responses vary among taxa, habitats, and regions. Because species responses are context-dependent, understanding how ecological characteristics and landscape history influence biodiversity distribution is essential for conservation planning. Objectives We evaluated how nearly two centuries of LULC change have influenced vertebrate distribution dynamics across Texas, USA, a landscape of biogeographic crossroads. We tested whether habitat specialization, taxonomic identity, conservation status, and ecoregional context better explain range expansion, contraction, and redistribution than landscape change metrics alone. Methods We compared historical and contemporary distributions of 100 native vertebrate species (mammals, birds, reptiles, and amphibians). Multi-temporal LULC datasets (1850–2023) were integrated with species occurrences, habitat associations, and ecoregional data to identify drivers of distribution range change. Results LULC change was spatially heterogeneous, driven by agricultural expansion, cropland abandonment, shrubland encroachment, and urbanization. Most species shifted ranges, with responses varying by habitat, taxon, and ecoregion. articles.title: Impacts of needle-leaved forests landscape pattern and environmental factors on the spatial differentiation of pine wilt disease in China
articles.desc: Following its emergence in China, pine wilt disease (PWD) has continuously expanded, creating substantial risks to regional forest ecosystems. However, most existing research emphasizes climate and other macro-scale associated factors, and lacks long-term and systematic analysis approached through the lens of forest landscape patterns. The research focuses on describing the spatiotemporal dynamics of PWD in China across the period 1982–2020 and identifying the dominant factors influencing its distribution. We specifically examined how needle-leaved forest landscape patterns interact with environmental conditions to shape the spread of PWD across regions. We applied the optimal parameters-based geographical detector (OPGD) model to analyze the spatial differentiation of PWD outbreaks. Needle-leaved forest landscape metrics and environmental variables were integrated to evaluate their individual and combined effects on disease spread. PWD has progressively expanded over the past four decades. The epidemic was primarily distributed along the southeastern coastal zones and subsequently extended toward the northwestern interior. articles.title: Spatial distribution and environmental drivers of wild honey bee nesting patterns in the Eastern Cape Province, South Africa
articles.desc: Spatial clusters of animal nests can be driven by mating behaviors, social benefits, and landscape heterogeneity. Unmanaged honey bees (Hymenoptera: Apidae: Apis spp.) have been documented nesting in clustered spatial distributions. However, environmental features influencing unmanaged honey bee nesting patterns have been largely understudied, especially for wild honey bees ( A. mellifera ) across Africa. We worked in the Eastern Cape Province, South Africa to characterize the spatial distribution and environmental drivers of wild honey bee nesting patterns. We surveyed 1 km 2 grid cells for wild honey bee nests using beelining techniques, with which we followed foragers from stands with sugar water to their nest entrances. We used nest locality data to test for complete spatial randomness using Monte Carlo simulations with mean nearest-neighbor distances. We used generalized linear mixed-effects models and a model selection approach to explore impacts of 11 land management, vegetation, and terrain covariates on patterns of nest density (nests/0.25 km 2 ). We located 97 occupied nests within 16 km 2 across five field sites. Wild honey bee colonies nested in both clustered and random spatial patterns. articles.title: Cross-scale influences of habitat and urbanisation on terrestrial vertebrates in coastal wetlands
articles.desc: Context Biodiversity in wetlands is impacted by expanding and intensifying urbanisation. While aquatic species spatial use of mangroves and saltmarshes is well established, little is known about how terrestrial vertebrates use these habitats in Australia and under what contexts. Objectives We surveyed terrestrial vertebrates in mangroves and saltmarshes in a diversity of estuarine seascapes, scaling from areas with extensive nearby urbanisation to more natural areas, and quantified the relative influence of habitat structure and composition, and landscape configuration on assemblage structure. Methods We surveyed terrestrial vertebrates using baited camera traps deployed for 48 h (i.e., four tidal cycles) across seven estuaries and 115 sites (57 mangrove and 58 saltmarsh) in southeast Queensland, Australia. articles.title: Landscape composition and photoperiod shape differences in space use and hunting behaviour between boreal and Alpine pygmy owl populations
articles.desc: Context Investigating how habitat specialists express population-level differences in habitat preferences and movement behaviour across contrasting landscapes and abiotic environments allows us to distinguish patterns that are consistent across populations from those that are population-specific responses to local conditions. Objectives We examined space use, hunting habitat selection and diel activity between Eurasian Pygmy Owl ( Glaucidium passerinum ) populations occupying boreal (south-west Finland) and subalpine (Western Italian Alps) forests, to assess the consistency of these patterns across regions with contrasting landscape structure and photoperiod. articles.desc: Context Urbanization transforms natural ecosystems into heterogeneous and fragmented landscapes, creating novel selective pressures that can drive eco-evolutionary dynamics. However, the specific role of urban spatial structure in shaping these dynamics remains poorly understood in landscape ecology. We evaluate the model using a plant–pollinator system to examine how these spatial properties influence extinction timing and mutualistic feedbacks under scenarios with and without plant trait evolution. articles.title: How do green space cooling benefits align with population needs? A multi-dimensional assessment in a land–water mosaic city
articles.desc: The cooling efficiency of green spaces exhibits intra-urban spatial heterogeneity, yet systematic assessments of how greenness, benefiting population size, and other environmental factors affect this efficiency remain scarce. Taking Wuhan as a case study, this research proposes an integrated framework to elucidate how green space cooling benefits align with population needs and to explain the underlying environmental drivers of spatial variations in cooling efficiency. The coupled WRF-UCM model was employed to measure changes in the Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI) between vegetated and non-vegetated scenarios. Cooling efficiency was highest in upwind southwestern regions and the western Yangtze Riverbank, and was lowest in downwind northwestern areas. articles.title: Identifying important areas for connectivity today and into the future: a spatial synthesis
articles.desc: Context Promoting landscape connectivity to support species movement has long been a key conservation strategy, one that is increasingly important as species move to track shifting climatic conditions. Connectivity modelers have developed a multitude of methods to identify important areas for providing connectivity in general or connectivity specifically to address climate change, and each resulting map has its own assumptions, uncertainties, and targets. Making decisions and conducting spatial planning with such diverse and often contradictory maps poses a significant challenge. Objectives Our objective was to synthesize both climate-connectivity and non-climate connectivity studies to identify areas of joint importance. Specifically, we 1) identified areas of agreement among climate connectivity maps, 2) identified areas of agreement among non-climate connectivity maps, and 3) identified areas jointly prioritized by both climate- and non-climate connectivity maps that may help species move both in the present and as the climate changes. We also asked secondary questions regarding the spatial distribution of mapping efforts, and whether climate- and non-climate connectivity maps are correlated with patterns of elevation and human modification in the region. articles.title: Hydrogeological constraints amplify phenological responses of karst vegetation to climate variability relative to non-karst vegetation
articles.desc: Geological background remains an overlooked regulator of vegetation phenological responses to climate change. articles.desc: Context Habitat loss and fragmentation are among the most significant drivers of biodiversity decline worldwide. Therefore, understanding the spatial movements of animals in fragmented landscapes is essential to determine habitat protection priorities. Objectives We aimed to investigate how variation in landscape configuration affects the home range size of breeding Carnaby’s cockatoos (CC) ( Zanda latirostris ), an endangered species facing multiple threats to their survival. We then calculated landscape metrics for each site and used linear regression to investigate how variation in landscape configuration and fragmentation affects home range size. articles.desc: Supply–demand imbalance of ecosystem services (ES) is a core challenge under rapid urbanization. Multi-scenario land-use simulation is widely used to explore coordination pathways, yet how alternative pathways reshape ES supply–demand equilibrium along the urban–rural gradient remains poorly understood. This study quantified how policy-oriented land-use pathways reshape ES supply–demand relationships across the urban–rural gradient, and located the spatial shift of their equilibrium point. articles.desc: Wildfires are a major ecological driver impacting terrestrial ecosystems, yet their belowground impacts remain poorly understood in Central European temperate forests. We investigated soil microbial responses during the first post-fire year following the large 2022 wildfire in the Bohemian and Saxon Switzerland National Parks (Czechia and Germany). However, effects of disease on both its production and spatial distribution are not well understood. We examined the effects of a dieback disease on leaf litterfall in forests dominated by a susceptible foundation tree species Agathis australis (kauri). Using leaf litterfall data and mapped trees from stands of varying successional stages and disease severity, we parameterised a spatially explicit Bayesian inverse model to estimate species-specific leaf litter production and dispersal for eight focal species as functions of tree size, distance from trunk, and disease severity. articles.title: Sociodemographic Factors and Land Use Shape Perceptions of Ecosystem Services in Reservoirs of Semiarid Regions
articles.desc: Community perceptions of ecosystem services are shaped by individuals’ local contexts and their direct interactions with the environment. Examining these relationships enables a better understanding of how human perceptions of ecosystem services are associated with anthropogenic environmental change. In this study, we assessed the relationship between ecosystem service perceptions in riverside communities of semiarid reservoirs and sociodemographic variables, as well as the extent to which different land uses and land covers influence these perceptions. Interviews were conducted with residents living along the margins of the Sumé, Poções, and Cordeiro reservoirs (Paraíba River Basin) and the Sabugí, Passagem das Traíras, and Cruzeta reservoirs (Piranhas-Açu River Basin) in Northeast Brazil. Overall, 84% of the ecosystem services perceived by respondents were provisioning services, 12% were cultural services, and only 4% were regulation and maintenance services. Nevertheless, reservoirs surrounded by larger forested areas presented higher proportions of perceived regulation and maintenance services, whereas those with greater human occupation showed higher proportions of perceived provisioning services. articles.desc: Elephants were a major driver of tree stem mortality in Africa, but their impacts are now spatially constrained and they no longer topple trees across the continent. Drift, selection and recombination bias drive the evolution of a non-ribosomal peptide
articles.desc: Non-ribosomal peptides play important roles in microbial ecology and medicine, for example as toxins and antibiotics such as penicillin. Like ordinary proteins, non-ribosomal peptides are subject to evolutionary change, which is driven by rampant recombinations of their synthetases. The evolutionary dynamics and causes of non-ribosomal peptide diversification are not well understood, because recombinations complicate phylogenetic analysis and statistical tests for natural selection and drift. Here we study the non-ribosomal GameXPeptides, which entomopathogenic bacteria use to kill their insect prey. We use recombination-aware phylogenetics, ancestral sequence reconstruction and statistical analysis of historical recombination patterns to retrace the evolution of GameXPeptides. This uncovers dozens of new GameXPeptides, including striking patterns of structural convergence. We provide statistical and experimental evidence that this diversity is shaped by selection, but also that GameXPeptides experience substantial genetic drift and biased recombination rates that limit the space of accessible peptide variants. Our work illuminates the complex interplay of adaptive and non-adaptive evolutionary forces acting on some of the most versatile chemical weapons in nature.

articles.desc: Adaptive plant development is orchestrated, among other means, by directional, intercellular transport of the phytohormone auxin. Self-organizing phenomena such as flexible vasculature formation depend on auxin canalization, which manifests as the gradual formation of auxin-transporting channels through feedback between auxin signalling and transport. Here we identify MAKR6 as a component of this feedback. MAKR6 transcripts accumulate in vascular cells and are tightly regulated by auxin via the Aux/IAA–ARF–WRKY23 transcriptional cascade. MAKR6 is required for auxin canalization-dependent processes, including leaf venation, vascular regeneration and de novo channel formation from local auxin sources. Mechanistically, MAKR6 interacts with the PIN1 auxin transporter and modulates its trafficking and polarization. MAKR6 also associates with and integrates TMK1/4 and CAMEL–CANAR, two key receptor-like kinase complexes involved in canalization. Together, our study establishes MAKR6 as a multifaceted regulator that couples transcriptional auxin signalling to PIN1 repolarization and coordinates multiple RLK-mediated pathways into a concerted process. This provides mechanistic insight into auxin canalization and exemplifies a framework for exploring similar regulatory nodes in other developmental contexts.

articles.title: Assembly-graph-assisted haplotype-resolved scaffolding of polyploid genomes
articles.desc: Assembling polyploid genomes at the chromosome level remains a major challenge due to the difficulty of accurately distinguishing homologous chromosomes, leaving a vast number of polyploid species without high-quality genome sequences. Current chromatin conformation capture (3C)-based haplotype-resolved scaffolding methods often produce highly incomplete and mis-phased assemblies of complex polyploids, as short sequences lacking sufficient interaction support and collapsed regions with misleading signals are difficult to resolve. Here we present GPhase, a haplotype-resolved scaffolding algorithm that integrates 3C (for example, Hi-C, Pore-C and Omni-C) data with assembly graphs to enhance accuracy, completeness and contiguity. By leveraging graph connectivity derived from long-read overlaps, GPhase effectively overcomes key limitations of 3C. When applied to 15 complex polyploid genomes, GPhase reduced the sequence missing rate (BUSCO-based) by up to tens-fold, decreased the sequence error rate (k-mer-based) by up to an order of magnitude and improved the contiguity (N50) of gap-free sequences by several-fold compared with existing tools.
